chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about gold, how much zakat is due upon it? He said: 'When its value reaches two hundred dirhams, zakat is due upon it.' There is no contradiction in this report with what we previously stated, that the nisab (minimum threshold) is twenty dinars, because he (peace be upon him) informed about the value of the time, and at that time the value of one dinar was ten dirhams. Do you not see that in many places regarding diyat (blood money) and other matters, they considered ten dirhams in exchange for one dinar, and made the choice between them on an equal basis? Thus is the ruling of this report, because the value of two hundred dirhams comes to be twenty dinars according to what we previously stated, and that which he narrated.

key_terms.قِيمَةُ الْوَقْتِ: Value of the time (contemporary exchange rate)

ai.seo_question: What is the nisab (minimum threshold) for zakat on gold according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent discrepancy between the gold and silver nisab thresholds by demonstrating that the Prophet’s statement regarding two hundred dirhams was based on the contemporary market value where one dinar equaled ten dirhams. This contextualization highlights the Shia scholarly principle of distinguishing between fixed weight-based standards and their fluctuating monetary equivalents, ensuring the zakat obligation remains consistent regardless of currency valuation shifts.
